title: Therapeutic alliance research utilizing physiologic synchrony in therapy
summary:
The study investigates how the therapeutic relationship and the synchronisation of heart rate variability (HRV, measured via ECG) between different dyads and in different constellations develop over time. The study involves not only the therapy seekers and the therapists, but also other relevant persons, such as parents of children or students, who play a role in the course of therapy.  It also examines how these aspects affect the therapy results in the analysed outcomes. The focus is primarily on the perception of the relationship between patients and therapists as well as their cooperation on a physical level, defined via HRV synchronisation.
In addition, general psychological stress, depressive symptoms, self-esteem, the ability to deal with feelings, the perception of stress and attachment dimensions are observed. The study is conducted over the entire period of therapy in order to visualise changes and correlations during the therapy process.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Participation is possible for all patients, therapists, any accompanying persons and students, within the framework of internships or BQT 3, of the outpatient clinic for children and adolescents at the University of Konstanz.
Exclusion criteria:
Suffering from physical illnesses and taking medication are generally not seen as exclusion criteria, but are taken into account in the analyses.
Due to the employment status at the university outpatient centre, therapists' health data is not recorded. For this reason, therapists are asked not to take part in the study if they suffer from illnesses or take medication that could affect the cardiovascular system.
Further exclusion criteria are acute danger to self or others and dependence syndrome (F1x.2) at the start of treatment.
